item.title: I slept in the room where Lizzie Borden's stepmom was killed. Here's what I found.
item.description: In 2019, a brave team of "48 Hours producers" traveled to Fall River, Massachusetts, to spend the night in the house where Andrew and Abby Borden were found brutally murdered.

item.title: Will the AI Bubble Hit Your Wallet? | Money Moves with Jill Schlesinger
item.description: Artificial intelligence is on everyone's lips these days—but what does it actually mean for your wallet? Jill and Mark are breaking down what you need to know about AI and your portfolio, including how to protect yourself from potential market turmoil. Plus, Jill and Mark help caller Cody prepare for a major career shift.

item.title: Ross Fire 100% contained after more than 3 weeks
item.description: The wildfire, which has torn through Palo Pinto and Jack counties, forced evacuations, closed roads and disrupted schools.

item.title: 2 adults and child found dead after flooding inundates New Mexico
item.description: Navajo Nation President Buu Nygren thanked first responders for working through the night in difficult and dangerous conditions as they searched for the people.

item.title: There are more trucks on highways. But the government is inspecting them less.
item.description: A CBS News investigation finds that nearly 600 people have died in crashes since 2024 with trucks operated by companies that had never been subjected to a roadside safety inspection.

item.title: 9th woman found dead in South Africa, adding to fears of serial killer
item.description: South African police say a ninth woman's body has been discovered in an area east of Johannesburg, adding that it could be linked to a series of killings they are investigating.

item.title: Millionaires are everywhere in the U.S., new book says
item.description: Getting rich in the U.S. is still possible, but the most common path to wealth doesn't involve working for other people, according to a new book.

item.title: OpenAI reveals 6 more incidents of "unexpected or concerning" AI behavior
item.description: OpenAI has disclosed six reports of "unexpected or concerning" behavior in artificial intelligence models as the debate on AI safety​ becomes increasingly heated.

item.title: House speaker declares Iran nuclear issue "taken care of"
item.description: The Iran war has cost the U.S. military at least $33.4 billion — most of it on munitions — and not including hundreds of millions more spent by other agencies, the Pentagon says.

item.title: 3 dead after NBC Los Angeles news helicopter crashes in Chatsworth
item.description: NBCLA identified the two victims on board the helicopter as aerial news reporter Eliana Moreno and pilot George Marciniw.

item.title: 5 missing women are linked to Olney home in Philadelphia. Here's what we know.
item.description: Inside the home, owned by Eugene Horsch and connected to his father, R.C. Horsch, authorities have found a trove of digital images, a so-called laboratory of chemicals and a small marijuana grow operation.

item.title: Patrick Clancy sits down with 60 Minutes
item.description: Patrick Clancy spoke with 60 Minutes this week. Shanelle Kaul has a preview of the story, which airs Sunday.

item.title: Details on Ed Sheeran tour as all acts quit after Macklemore dropped for pro-Palestine comments
item.description: Ed Sheeran is facing intense public backlash after rapper Macklemore, who was set to open his upcoming tour dates, was dropped from the production over pro-Palestine comments. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul reports and Alex Suskind, news director at online music magazine Pitchfork, joins "The Daily Report" to discuss.

item.title: House passes Russia sanctions bill, overcoming Democratic opposition
item.description: The bill was championed by GOP Sen. Lindsey Graham, who died suddenly just one day after announcing a deal had been reached with the White House to move forward.

item.title: Federal agencies spent $9.5 billion on salary costs for administrative leave in 2025
item.description: A new report from the Government Accountability Office shows federal agencies spent $9.5 billion on administrative leave costs in 2025, an increase spurred by the DOGE push to cut down the federal workforce. CBS News' Aaron Navarro has more.

item.title: Coast Guard and FBI boarded tankers due to cyberattacks. How big is the risk?
item.description: U.S. Coast Guard personnel and FBI agents boarded two Texas-bound energy tankers last month after cyberattacks struck the vessels while they were traveling toward the United States, according to U.S. officials.

item.title: Federal Reserve raises interest rates for the first time since 2023
item.description: The Fed increased its benchmark rate by 0.25 percentage points to battle resurgent inflation driven by soaring energy prices.

item.title: When an intruder invaded a golden retriever's home, he just tried to play
item.description: A golden retriever got his big chance to be a guard dog, but instead of guarding, Nash tried to play with the intruder. Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: Video shows first responders rushing to flame-engulfed motel, saving lives
item.description: Newly released video shows fire ripping through a Florida motel this weekend and first responders rushing into the danger. Cristian Benavides spoke with two of them.

item.title: North Carolina GOP Senate nominee Michael Whatley reacts to farmer's criticism of tariffs, gas costs
item.description: President Trump is traveling to North Carolina to stump for Republican Senate nominee Michael Whatley. CBS News chief White House correspondent Nancy Cordes spoke with Whatley ahead of the president's appearance.

item.title: House passes late Sen. Lindsey Graham's Russia sanctions bill, sending it to Trump's desk
item.description: The House on Wednesday evening passed a Russia sanctions bill championed by the late Sen. Lindsey Graham. CBS News congressional reporter Taurean Small has the latest.

item.title: The races to watch with balance of power in Congress up for grabs
item.description: CBS News' director of elections and surveys Anthony Salvanto breaks down the congressional races to watch ahead of the midterm elections.

item.title: House passes bill to shield Americans from data center energy costs
item.description: The vote comes as lawmakers face increasing pressure to respond to the data center boom driven by the AI race.

item.title: Florida Democratic governor hopeful David Jolly says politics are at a "1974 post-Watergate moment"
item.description: Democrats are bullish this election cycle, even eyeing the governor's mansion in President Trump's adopted home state of Florida. The nominee, David Jolly, faces an uphill battle as Democrats haven't won a statewide race in the Sunshine State since 2018. Jolly joins "The Takeout" to discuss his campaign.

item.title: Feds paid $9.5 billion in leave costs in 2025 due to DOGE buyout
item.description: According to a Government Accountability Office (GAO) report published Tuesday, the use of paid administrative leave increased by 435% from 2023 to 2025.

item.title: 9/16: CBS Evening News
item.description: Patrick Clancy sits down with 60 Minutes; Details on news helicopter crash, killing 3.

item.title: Alabama attorney general candidate says AI could mark "new chapter" of legal action against Big Tech
item.description: House lawmakers are heading home for recess until after the midterms, leaving artificial intelligence regulation still stalled in Congress. Alabama Republican candidate for attorney general Katherine Robertson, who is currently leading a state investigation into OpenAI, joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Expert: Images of damaged U.S. bases in Middle East show Iran "getting help from Russia and China"
item.description: CBS News has exclusively gained access to photos that show widespread damage at U.S. bases in the Middle East as a result of the war with Iran. Former Defense Department official Matthew Kroenig joins "The Takeout" with his reaction.

item.title: NASA spacecraft discovers moon crater bigger than Roman Colosseum
item.description: Scientists have discovered a crater on the moon that's bigger than the Roman Colosseum, the result of a powerful impact two years ago.

item.title: Is the U.S. and China's mutual distrust the biggest risk as AI evolves?
item.description: Analysts tell CBS News that as the U.S. and China race for AI supremacy, they risk driving all of humanity "off a cliff."
